To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Enteric nematode infections are associated with changes in intestinal glucose metabolism, which are macrophage dependent, and that the macrophage response to infection is a key determinant of the type of glucose transporters that are expressed by the epithelial cell.
macrophages are necessary to reduce the activity of sodium-linked glucose transporters and to down-regulate GLUT2 expression during enteric nematodal infection.

macrophages are required for the inhibition of SGLT1 glucose transporter activity and the down-regulation of the GLUT2 glucose transporter, but are not required for the increased paracellular permeability of the epithelium during a type 2 inflammatory response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the host immune system interacts with the enteric epithelium to alter its physiology.
the mechanisms of altered epithelial function during nematode-induced type 2 immune responses.
understanding how the host immune response to nematodes influences the function of the enteric mucosal epithelium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the role of Mϕ during a Th2 immune response induced by enteric Nematode infection includes the following: (1) inhibition of SGLT1-mediated glucose absorption, (2) inhibition of GLUT2-mediated glucose uptake and (3) up-regulation of GLUT1-mediated glucose absorption.
macrophage activation is an important component of the type 2 immune responses to nematode infection, which is associated with altered epithelial glucose absorption and epithelial barrier function.

the role of macrophages in the epithelial function during a type 2 response induced by enteric nematod infection is to reduce the activity of the sodium-dependent glucose transporter, SGLT1, but not the glucose transporter GLUT2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the enteric immune response induced by nematodes is characterized by a macrophage-driven inhibition of sodium-linked sugar transport, a macrophage-mediated decrease in glucose transporter 2, and an up-regulation in glucose transporter 1.
the type 2 immune responses induced by nematode infection have a major impact on the function of the intestinal epithelium.
the type 2 immune system is not only a major contributor to host resistance to infection, but is a key regulator of glucose absorption in the intestine.
The main takeaway from our work is that

macrophages play a role in the inhibition of glucose absorption during enteric nematodiasis, and the inhibition is mediated by a reduction in the activity of the sodium-linked glucose transporter SGLT1.
macrophages play a key role in the altered glucose absorption and epithelial function that occurs during nematode induced inflammation.
macrophages play a critical role in the altered glucose metabolism of the enterocytes during a type 2 response to nematode infection.
